# External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log, November 1-15, 2026

Archive for November 1-15, 2026. Discovery passes appear newest first. The [current sweep log](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog) carries the most recent passes.

Archive: [October 16-31, 2026](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog-2026-10b)

## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Midday Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, seven hours after the night pass. The canonical grew by **18** slugs with **0** removals and the submission window carried **8** arrivals, but the finding of this window is a billing design rather than a product category.

- [ListRiver MCP - US Business Registry Data as a Lead List](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/listriver-mcp/) - package `listriver-mcp` **0.1.0** over stdio, registry record `io.github.ListRiver-LLC/listriver` active since `2026-11-03T13:24:59Z`. A keyless `initialize` answers **200** as `ListRiver` **0.1.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` and returns all three tool schemas plus the server's own instruction set; `tools/call` then returns the documented **401** naming `LISTRIVER_API_KEY`, so the surface is fully readable before a credential exists. Three tools: `list_states`, `count_businesses`, `search_businesses`. **The first two are free and the third spends records**, which is the whole reason the entry exists: every other business-data server in this catalogue makes you learn the size of a market by buying the pull, and here an agent sizes a market, narrows it on `has_phone`, `has_email`, `naics`, `entity_type` and `formed_within`, and only then retrieves names, with a cursor to continue rather than restart. Records are **filings, not profiles**: address, county, registered agent and formation month, plus phone, email, website, EIN and NAICS where the state publishes them, which makes **a business filed last month** a prospect with no website to audit and no ad history to bid against. Two limits come from the server itself and are recorded as the two ways this surface can mislead: phone, email, NAICS and county coverage is **partial and state-dependent**, and the server instructs the agent to check with `count_businesses` before promising a phone list; and the records carry a use restriction barring **credit, insurance, employment or housing** decisions, which is the FCRA boundary stated plainly. Free tier **500** records a calendar month, then **$50** for 5,000 rising to **$450** for 75,000, with prepaid packs and an AWS Marketplace path; the record is the unit and every re-returned business counts again. No overlap with [Corply](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/corply-mcp/) (a formation service), [Leadbay](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/leadbay-mcp/) or [Vibe Prospecting](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vibe-prospecting-mcp/) (proprietary scoring) or [firmy.ai](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/firmy-ai-mcp/) (Polish KRS, one country).

## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Night Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening pass. Both named surfaces were quiet and this time the quiet is measurable rather than asserted: the mcpservers.org twelve-sitemap canonical returned **20,000** distinct server URLs from **63,359** raw `<loc>` entries across the same **12** server maps, **set identical** to the 21:00 capture with **0 additions and 0 removals**, and the mcp.so homepage carried **one** card above the evening stamp, **PendingDelete.net** at `2026-11-08T08:56:02.072Z`, on both the plain and the cache-busted read. The submission queue carried **12** arrivals from `#6923` to `#6935` with `#6932` absent.

**One server was catalogued**, and it is the only arrival in twelve whose job is not already done by an entry here.

- [DutyKit MCP - The Compliance Gate Before an Agent Acts](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dutykit-mcp/) - keyless `initialize` **200** on `https://dutykit.dev/mcp` as `dutykit` **0.1.0**, no account and no key, **five** tools and all five called live. Three of them are pre-checks on an action rather than lookups: `werbung_vorpruefen` (may this email or call go out, § 7 UWG), `rechnung_vorpruefen` (§ 14 Abs. 4 UStG fields), `vat_pruefen` (live VIES), plus `pflichten`, an obligation catalogue for DE, LU and EU-wide duties with legal basis, source URL, check date and verification status on every line, and `ki_hinweis`, the AI Act Art. 50 Abs. 1 wording in de, fr, en and lb. **The verdict is three-valued:** `erlaubt: false` for a consumer email with no documented consent under § 7 Abs. 2 UWG, and `erlaubt: null` with "human approval required" for the business-customer exception under § 7 Abs. 3 UWG, so the ambiguous case goes to a person instead of reading as a pass. Every answer carries a `nachweis` with a timestamp, the tool, a `verantwortlich` field and a **SHA-256** of the result. Driven live: `vat_pruefen` on `LU26375245` returned `gueltig: true` with **AMAZON EUROPE CORE S.A R.L.** as VIES holds it; `pflichten` for `DE` + `online_handel` returned three obligations with **EUR 25,000** / **EUR 100,000** small-business thresholds and each marked `belegt` and checked `2026-11-07`; `rechnung_vorpruefen` refused a thin invoice with eight named missing fields and stated its own boundary (no EN 16931 format check). Free public beta at **200** calls a day per IP, no stored inputs in the free tier; MIT code, CC BY 4.0 catalogue; repository **0** stars, created `2026-11-08T09:23:40Z`, size **0 KB**, recorded as a limit. Output is German apart from `ki_hinweis`. Not a duplicate of [EU VAT VIES](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/honest-vies-mcp/), [Rechnungslotse](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/rechnungslotse-mcp/) or [EU AI Act Explorer](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/eu-ai-act-explorer-mcp/): those are references, this one is called instead of acting and returns a verdict with a hash.

**Held with the class owner named.** **OfferMagnet Jobs** (`io.offermagnet/jobs`) on the jobs class owned by [FoundRole](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/foundrole-mcp/), which already fact-checks visa sponsorship on every posting; driven keyless **200** with five tools. **LocalProspects** on the local-business lead class carried by [Google Maps Scraper](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/google-maps-scraper-mcp/), with owner names and phone-carrier enrichment over live Maps data, **401** keyless. **1ClickWebsite** on the WordPress and site-builder class carried by [WordPress.com](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/wordpress-com-mcp/), **401** keyless. **QuassLabs API** as agent and delivery tooling: **32** deterministic linters, scorers and calculators, keyless `initialize` **200** and `tools/call` refused for a missing key. **Power Players** as a civic vertical, keyless **200** with ten tools over US officials and crowdsourced ratings. **Billigast** on the regional consumer class set by the same author's Blocket MCP. **EasyTranscriber** on the transcript class. **Vectorial Data Terminal** on the saturated trading class, **AgentX** and **MCP Security Scanner** as agent infrastructure, and **whoelse** as research tooling. From the mcp.so card, **PendingDelete.net** on the domain class carried by [Expired Domains](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/expired-domains-mcp/).

**Core listing check, measured.** The fresh canonical carries `/servers/corpusiq-io` and `/servers/corpusiq/corpusiq-docs`; mcpservers.org `/all` answers **403**, the standing edge policy; on mcp.so the namespaced slug `/servers/corpusiq/multi-source-mcp` now answers **307** to `https://mcp.so/server/multi-source-mcp/corpusiq`, which answers **404**, and the four direct slugs all answer **404**, so the listing remains absent and the redirect is a routing change rather than a change of state; Glama answers **200** on the connector route.

## 🆕 November 7, 2026 - Evening Sweep (4 New, 4 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the supplement and six hours after any pass had read every surface, and the largest surface moved this time: the mcpservers.org twelve-sitemap universe went from **19,898** distinct server URLs at 11:00 to **20,000**, from **63,359** raw `<loc>` entries across **12** server maps with **43,344** inline locale prefixes stripped. The submission queue carried **19** arrivals from `#6902` to `#6922`.

**Four servers were catalogued**, and all four are about an agent being handed evidence it can check rather than prose it has to trust.

- [PointRover MCP - The Supply Chain Board for One Business](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pointrover-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://pointrover.com/mcp`, keyless `initialize` **401** naming its discovery document, and that document answers **200** with one scope (`read:tenant`). **Nine read-only tools** over a per-business board built in about an hour and checked every twelve hours: inputs and what moves upstream of them, import duties by product and country with Section 232 and 301, federal and state rules in the regulator's own words, the wage in the owner's town, county demographics and customer travel, and the recalls, weather alerts and trade actions that reach it. `pointrover_changes_since` returns only what moved since a `board_version`, and `pointrover_receipt` returns the record behind a single figure. **$79** a business a month after a 14-day trial, **$59** from the third and **$49** from the tenth. Not a duplicate of [Tariff Monitor](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tariff-monitor-mcp/): that is a local HTS duty calculator, this is a per-business record with receipts.
- [Patchwell MCP - Clean Data, Cited Research, Transcribed Audio](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/patchwell-mcp/) - keyless `initialize` **200** as `Patchwell` **1.30.0** with **five** tools. Cleaning returns `stats`, a before-and-after quality score (**0.30** to **0.998** on the vendor's 352-row sample), a per-change log of row, column, before, after and rule, and a replayable recipe; research puts a source link on each sentence and lists what it could not confirm; transcription returns word timings, speaker labels and every hallucination-guard removal. **$0.008** an audio minute, **$0.50** per 1,000 rows, **$0.15** a research answer, **$1** of free credit with no card.
- [DeskHand MCP - The CRM an Agent Can Be Trusted to Run](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/deskhand-mcp/) - keyless `initialize` **200** as `deskhand` **1.0.0** with **30** tools and a policy preamble the server writes for the agent. One key per agent with scopes, its own rate limit and daily send cap; an append-only audit log with before and after; revert one action or a whole run; approval as a switch per agent; a built-in `dry_run` identity and `simulate_campaign` before `launch_campaign` refuses on named blockers. **Free** during early access, **EUR 19** a month on Pro.
- [eDiscovery Decoder MCP - Review Statistics You Can Defend](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ediscovery-decoder-mcp/) - keyless `initialize` **200** as `ediscovery-decoder-news-calc` **0.1.0** with **15** tools, **13** of them usable. Deterministic review statistics: recall from a confusion matrix, elusion, sample size, TAR recall estimate, prevalence and richness, control-set recall, cutoff comparison and validation-plan QC. Free, no account, aggregate counts only, stated by the vendor as an educational non-commercial preview.

**Held with the class owner named.** `a1lane-ai-docs-mcp` on the saturated social publishing class (UniPost, ViewsBase, Postkey, FeedSquad, Sendcove); `emailwarmup-bobwork-ai-api` on Warmerly's outbound class; `lexpact-co-uk-developers-docs` on UK contract generation; `mutalaa-tr-ictihat-arama` on the regional legal class from October; the four `illyism` packs as one single-author fleet on AI-search visibility, backlinks, slides and tooling; `adplug-app-integrations-meta-ads` and `adwarp-dev/adwarp` on ads intelligence; eight media-generation slugs on the Varosity and MakeMidas class; twenty-one developer and agent-infrastructure slugs (work handoff over ACP, REST bridge, FigJam context, JSON repair, tool linting, multi-model fan-out, CDN, goal maps, self-hosted search, calendar arithmetic, offline dictation, storage sync, pay-per-call marketplace, registry statistics); `api-lilambd-com-mcp` on the Apify-actor distribution hold; `jefferyleo/ezverify-mcp` and `mailveri-mcp` on email verification; `www-linkjolt-io-developers-mcp` on affiliate operations; and the consumer and vertical remainder. ## 🆕 November 7, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **11:00 MST** tick, one hour after the midday pass. The canonical did not move: **19,898** distinct server URLs came back from **14** documents and **76,632** raw `<loc>` entries, **0 additions and 0 removals** against the 10:00 capture, and the **40 additions with 1 removal** returned against the 03:00 baseline are exactly the midday pass's own window, so there was nothing to disposition a second time. The mcp.so homepage carried the same newest card at `2026-11-07T16:50:15.825Z` with **0** above it. The submission queue moved: **3** arrivals from `#6899` to `#6901`, filed between 10:08 and 10:51 MST.

- [DocPin MCP - Publish an Agent's HTML to a Link You Control](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/docpin-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.docpin.app/mcp`, OAuth with dynamic client registration and PKCE, documented from the server's own contract because there is no API key to drive. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** naming its protected-resource document, and that document answers **200** with exactly **2** scopes, `publish` and `settings`, which is the split that decides what a connection can do. **The stable link is the entry:** republishing a `slug` puts a new version **behind the same link**, and around it sit the four capabilities nobody on the artifact shelf combines - `set_access` with `team`, `public`, `password`, `people` (emails and `@domains`) or `inherit`, version history with `restore_version`, `get_page_views` reporting **by whom** on a people-only page, and a per-page JSON store that `set_page_data` updates **without republishing**. Sharing a draft requires an `access` value, so the agent has to ask who should be allowed in. Page data is capped at **1 MB** and about **30 writes a minute**; upload links live **15 minutes** and take **25 MB**; drafts preview for about an hour and are not for sharing. **Free** is 3 pages, **Pro $8 a month** adds unlimited pages, custom domains and password or people-only pages.
- [AgentKeyGate MCP - A Pass Instead of the API Key](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/agentkeygate-mcp/) - self-hosted gateway, Apache-2.0, Node.js 22, Streamable HTTP at `https://{host}/mcp` behind a `gwa_...` agent token, **1.0.2** in the registry. **The agent never receives the service key:** it asks for a pass with a `ttl` and a call count and a reason up to **200** characters, a person approves in Telegram or on the web with those facts in view, and the pass `gwt_...` dies when the clock or the calls run out. **The data filter is why it earns the guide:** types and fields are chosen explicitly and everything else is cut from the JSON **before it reaches the agent**, `readOnly` is **on by default for CRM and support keys**, blocked writes do not consume quota, and `mask` replaces e-mails, separated phones, Luhn-valid cards and IBANs. The vendor's own example: a Bitrix24 lead returns seven fields and the agent gets `ID`, `STATUS_ID` and `OPPORTUNITY`. Weakening a filter needs a **fresh TOTP code** and shows a "was, now" page first. Recorded honestly: **0 stars**, created **2026-11-05**, single owner, no external audit, root on the server reads every key, filtering exists for four services, and the vendor's own `Checked live` column reads **`no`** on every client snippet including the **Hermes** one.

**Held with the class owner named.** `#6900` **Blocket MCP** on the regional classifieds class carried by `marketplaces-mcp-ru`: a read-only server over Sweden's largest classifieds site across 13 sections with scam red flags and price comparison, no key and no login, in three distributions. Sound build, one country's consumer marketplace, no business-system data behind it. Its own registry search returned **0** records. Nothing held from the sitemap or from mcp.so, because neither surface produced a candidate.

**Count.** The guide tree held **1,113** directories before this pass and holds **1,115** after it, **1,256** entries before and **1,258** after.

## 🆕 November 7, 2026 - Night Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick six hours after the evening pass, and the sitemap was **flat**: **19,859** server URLs against **19,859**, **zero additions and zero removals**. A count is not a diff, so the proof here is arithmetic: this pass fetched **19,859** distinct server URLs, the last capture on record is **19,513**, the two November 6 passes account for **346** additions, and the diff against that baseline returned exactly **346** additions and **0** removals. A single new server would have made it 347. The window came instead from the mcp.so homepage, which put **2** cards above the evening stamp (`2026-11-07T02:31:44.172Z`), and from the submission queue, which added **15** numbers from `#6878` to `#6892`, all arrivals.

- [SumOffice MCP - Edit the Real xlsm and Get It Back](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/sumoffice-mcp/) - hosted remote server at `https://view.sumoffice.com/mcp`, `sumoffice-document` **0.3.0**, **21** tools, **no account and no key**, plus the same server as a Docker image for a local file over stdio. It opens a real `.docx`, `.xlsx` or `.xlsm` up to 50 MB in a private editor cabin, reads cells and formulas, the VBA project with its entry points and blockers, the Power Query steps and load targets, and the paragraphs, comments and tracked changes, proposes a change, applies it only on approval, and returns a copy as a 24-hour download link. **Driven on the read path:** the `cashflow` demo opened as a genuine `.xlsm` with three sheets, `vba_project: true`, two tables, one query table, one connection and `data_mashup: true`; `macro_list` returned `Module1.FlagCashGaps` user-runnable on the **native** route with no blockers and `Sheet1.Worksheet_Change` on the **excel-bridge** route blocked as an event-or-document module at line 12, without executing anything; `query_list` returned `MonthlyCashflow` with its load target and refresh state and **the M body withheld by engine policy with only its sha256 exposed**, which is the right call for the string that carries a connection credential. The round trip is the argument: the vendor's **20 September 2026** proof run opened an Enron workbook with a VBA project and a dynamic-array UDF, applied a proposed formula and saved a copy that Excel 16 opened with no repair dialog and `xl/vbaProject.bin` byte-identical. The write path refused twice in this session and both refusals are in the guide: `unsupported-cell-preview-edits` for plain numeric inputs, then `busy: all 5 editor cabins are in use`, the documented concurrency ceiling of the hosted server. It earns the entry beside the [Basis MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/basis-mcp/) engine catalogued the evening before: Basis recomputes and audits a workbook, SumOffice edits the file and ships the artifact back with its package parts intact.

**Provenance note worth keeping in the ledger.** This pass began on a catalogue clone three commits behind `origin/main`, which already carried that evening sweep and its two guides. Basis and CarbonMeld were therefore researched, probed and written up a second time, and the duplicate was caught only when the branch checkout refused because both guide directories already existed on the remote. - [ProveCart MCP - Agent Order Checks Before Payment](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/provecart-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.provecart.com/mcp`, keyless `initialize` **200** as `provecart` **1.0.2** with all **10** tools listed, and **the evidence tier stated rather than implied**: `provecart_scoreboard` and `provecart_certification_info` were called live and returned real payloads, while the three check tools refuse without an integrator key in the `X-API-Key` header and say so in one sentence, so the check payload is schema-read and not measured. `provecart_check_order`, `provecart_check_booking` and `provecart_check_reservation` compare what the agent built against the customer's own **mandate** and return a signed **MATCH**, **REVIEW** or **BLOCK** verdict before the payment is captured, with a non-MATCH answer carrying the Agent Correction Format - a `corrections` array of `dimension`, `action`, `expected`, `actual`, `reason`, a retry budget and a sealed evidence pointer. **The mandate is the part that makes this different from a prompt**: the order mandate carries **18** structured fields including `max_total_price`, `merchant_allowlist`, `merchant_blocklist`, `max_quantity`, `variant_constraints`, `price_basis`, `expires_at` and a `period_budget` with its own window, the booking mandate **26** including `airport_substitution`, `date_flex_days`, `fare_terms`, `max_connections`, `min_connection_minutes` and `max_layover_minutes`, and the reservation mandate **17** including `time_tolerance_minutes`, `party_size_max`, `max_deposit` and `cancellation`. The rules read live: **80** or above certifies, a pass is CURRENT for **90 days**, status is computed from the sealed record at read time, renewal is a newly generated exam, and a pass produces an Open Badges 3.0 / W3C Verifiable Credential under `did:web:api.provecart.com`. The limits are in the guide: it never holds or moves money, a verdict gates a payment only where the integrator's code calls the check first, the AI layer cannot overturn a block, business onboarding is a free **90-day** pilot rather than a published price, and `provecart.com` answers **401** to a plain reader-proxy fetch. - [lookfirst MCP - Human Approval Gate for Agent Writes](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/lookfirst-mcp/) - a local stdio MCP proxy, Apache-2.0 at `github.com/Aethelgard-Systems/lookfirst`, installed here from the repository and reporting `lookfirst 0.2.1` against a README that still says 0.2.0 pre-1.0. **Driven, not quoted:** the offline demo was run twice end to end. The approval run returned `{"status":"executed","approved_by":"elicitation:mcp","readback":"ok","readback_detail":"read-back matches","blocked":false}` and the fake bank balance moved **1,250.00 to 1,129.50 EUR** for a **120.50 EUR** transfer; the denial run returned `"status":"denied"` with the failed channel named and the balance untouched. Five behaviours are what earn the guide. **The decision fails closed and the default table is short**: `readOnlyHint` allows, `destructiveHint`, an unannotated write and an unknown tool all confirm, and an explicit rule beats the annotation while `deny` never executes. **The approval is bound to the arguments**: the webhook answer must carry the per-call HMAC token and echo `args_sha256` from the preview or it returns **403**, the web page binds its buttons the same way, and every channel shares one timeout where a timeout is a denial. **The write is verified by read-back** against `$args` and `$result` placeholders and reported as `ok`, `unklar` or `fehlgeschlagen`, with `structuredContent.lookfirst` carrying the verdict so a write is never reported as done on its own word. **The log is an Ed25519 hash chain**: `verify-log` walked the run to **OK, 20 signed and chained entries**, and the demo then rewrote the decision entry and the same command returned **TAMPERED, line 6, hash mismatch**, with the documented residual (end-truncation plus a deleted `.head` sidecar) closed by an external `--trusted-head` checkpoint. **The result is masked before the model sees it**: the agent received `[[IBAN_c30e2f3c...]]` and `[[NAME_5f082d93...]]`, passing the placeholder back works because the gate resolves it, and an invented one is refused with `Denied: unknown or expired placeholder`. The limits are the vendor's own and are in the guide: pre-1.0 with no field record, **0** stars, an autonomous client that auto-answers elicitation approves itself unless `confirm.elicitation` is off and the page is isolated at the network level, a separate OS user is not enough because every local user reaches loopback, the page has no login and is for `127.0.0.1`, an HTTP token is authentication rather than encryption, Windows is untested, and the mask is a deterministic pattern filter that misses split IBANs, zero-width text, Base64 secrets and keys like `db_password`. It earns a guide because [kosa8](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/kosa8-mcp/) isolates the server, TrustScan and AgentTrust judge an endpoint, and glc PromptGuard scores a prompt or an output, and **none of them stops one specific write at the argument level, names the human who approved it, verifies the result by reading it back and keeps a chain you can point at**.

Passive site-wide logging and active per-page submission receipts are different instruments, so both belong here. **A correction is recorded with the entry**: the guide's first version claimed the catalogue held the answer side of AI visibility and "the input side none", which was wrong, since IndexLinks has read verified crawler visits with timestamps since October 6 and the [AI Crawler Index](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pathwren-ai-crawler-index/) verifies crawler IPs against operator-published ranges; the guide now names both and explains what this entry adds instead of asserting the slice was missing. The limits are in the guide: it measures rather than controls, the vendor's own framing is visit records and policy signals rather than rankings or model-training proof, the free plan is **1** site and **100** crawl visits a month with crawl analysis only, and `llms.txt` coverage, sitemap coverage, bot authenticity and the crawl-like-a-bot simulation all start at **Pro, $20 a month**.

The operator writes a mandate with a `purpose`, a `default` and an ordered clause list where each clause carries an `effect` of `permit`, `deny` or `escalate`; the agent passes the mandate plus the action it is about to take, and the first matching clause decides. Every answer carried a `hanria-receipt-v1` receipt with the mandate digest, the action digest, an issue time, a fifteen-minute window and a signature. `validate_mandate` reports the three failures that make a policy decorative, clauses that can never run because an earlier clause already decides them, unbounded prefixes and credential material, and it proved strict by refusing a first attempt that used `kind` values of `payment` and `access` and a free-text clause field, naming the offending field and the accepted taxonomy of `file`, `process`, `package`, `network`, `device`, `credential_use`, `transaction` and `administrative`. ## 🆕 November 2, 2026 - Midday Supplement (1 New, 1 Guide)

An hour after the midday pass, fired on the 11:00 MST tick, so this is a supplement rather than a second midday read: the window, the feed and the `/all` page were already dispositioned an hour earlier and are not re-argued here. What changed in the hour is three submissions (`Publish MCP` **#6621**, `norc` **#6622**, `Lingard Vocab` **#6623**) and one reversal with a reason attached.

- [AttriKit MCP - App Attribution That Returns a Decision](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/attrkit-mcp/) - stdio through `npx -y @attrkit/mcp`, published as **2.0.1** on npm with the MIT repository `KamyarTaher/attrikit-mcp` whose README carries the full **39**-tool table, the MCP setup page carrying the same inventory and count, and the pricing page carrying its free allowance in the headline. It is the first entry here that closes the loop from ad spend to app install to subscription revenue to a budget decision. `get_campaign_decision` returns the attribution engine's call verbatim and the vendor states the model reports it rather than recomputing it; `record_campaign_decision` stores the scale, cut or hold call with the inputs that produced it, so the call can be graded later once enough results exist, with the vendor's own caveat that a suggestion is not a profit guarantee. Spend is an input rather than a copied dashboard: `import_spend` takes ad level CSV rows with the paired `adset_id`/`ad_id` rule enforced client side since 1.0.0, `pull_network_spend` reads an authorized ad account, `set_cost_model` records allocation, and `get_spend` returns it beside installs and events. RevenueCat joins purchases, renewals and refunds to installs. The delivery rules, the timeouts (15 seconds on most tools, 120 on `export_events`, `import_spend` and `pull_network_spend`), the version 1 export cut at the newest 100,000 events, the one-member workspace, the web SDK not yet on npm and the 25-month retention are all in the guide, as is the pricing read directly: first **10,000** qualified installs free once with no card, then **$249** a month including 10,000, then **$0.015** each, which prices 50,000 at **$849** and 100,000 at **$1,599**. It earns a guide because [Mobzio MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mobzio-mcp/) answers which link produced a marketplace order for a Russian and CIS seller and stops there, while the ad surfaces here stop at the creative ([Abyssale MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/abyssale-mcp/), [AdTest.AI MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adtest-mcp/), [Ad Library Intelligence MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ad-library-intelligence-mcp/), [Adspy MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adspy-mcp/), [AdMake AI MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/admake-ai-mcp/)), so no entry in **1,085** guides joined spend to installs and returned a decision with its inputs saved.

**Reversal, stated plainly.** The midday pass an hour earlier grouped `AttriKit` (`#6592`) with developer tooling and mobile attribution and held it there. That grouping is reversed here on the surface rather than on the vendor: mobile attribution had no catalogued class to be held against (`WarpLink` was listed as identified and never written up, and [Mobzio MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mobzio-mcp/) is marketplace deeplinks for one regional seller set), and the decision and spend tools are an operator surface, not a developer one. Seven hours after the early morning pass, and the two directory surfaces behaved in opposite ways. The mcp.so `recentServers` block carried **30** cards with a date and the newest at `2026-11-01T13:11:50Z`, so exactly **three** sat above the `2026-11-01T03:23:34Z` stamp: `maprouter-12eecf`, `knowra` and `socialfaktory-b87655`. The mcpservers.org `/all` newest page was read twice, and the first read was a **stale proxy snapshot**: it returned the counter at **18,726**, the same figure the early morning pass recorded, with the same thirty slugs and not one of them unledgered in a way that would have been true seven hours earlier. Three of the six were new to the tree, three resolved to prior dispositions, and the submission window **#6540** to **#6550** carried eleven more.

- [Royally MCP - WordPress Fleet Changes With Approvals](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/royally-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.royally.io/mcp`, carried in the official registry as `io.royally/royally` at version **0.0.898** with status **active** and `statusChangedAt` on **2026-11-01T04:1xZ**, and answering a keyless `initialize` with **HTTP 401** and `{"error":"missing_bearer_token"}`, so the surface is live and gated rather than absent. The shape is a cloud command layer plus a plugin on every site, so an agent holds one connection instead of twenty site endpoints. The change flow is the entry: a request is recorded with who asked and which sites it touches, held for approval inside a window that can expire, optionally behind two-person approval and per-site-group rules, applied, and returned as a receipt naming who asked, who approved, what changed on which site and the one click that puts it back, with the receipts collected in a fleet-wide tamper-evident log that exports signed. Safe jobs such as a cache purge after a menu edit are the documented exception and run without the queue. Around that the fleet jobs are worked through the plugins the sites already run: updates with a backup first and automatic rollback, vulnerability and administrator-change alerts through GuardPress, Wordfence or Kadence, backup health through SiteVault or UpdraftPlus, uptime every five minutes with certificate, domain, speed and PHP fatal error checks routed to Slack, Discord or a signed webhook, bulk SEO titles and descriptions and menu and CSS and template copies, WooCommerce prices and stock and orders with a seven-day undo, Elementor builds that wait for approval with a preview link first, SEO audits pulling Search Console and Analytics data through Rank Math and SEOSbolt, and weekly or monthly client reports in the agency's own brand beside a read-only client portal. Pricing read directly: Solo **$89 a year** for 3 sites and 2 seats, Freelancer **$249** for 5 sites and 3 seats, Studio **$390** for 25 sites and 5 seats. It earns a guide because every WordPress entry here is single-site, and because it is the first entry in this catalogue that governs **other MCP servers** rather than only its own tools: its documentation covers connecting the WordPress MCP Adapter, Easy MCP AI and the Elementor MCP behind the same connection under the stated rule that only Royally makes the change, which is supervision rather than a plugin list.

## 🆕 November 1, 2026 - Early Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Six hours after the night pass, and the two directories split cleanly: the mcp.so `recentServers` block put exactly **two** cards above the `2026-11-01T00:15:52Z` stamp, and mcpservers.org carried **30** slugs with the counter at **18,726** against **18,577**, every one of them already inside a prior disposition. The movement was in the submission window, where **eight** submissions landed between `#6531` at `04:46:00Z` and `#6539` at `10:02:34Z`. Three shipped, and each was verified on the surface it actually exposes, which for one of them is a keyless read-only sibling server rather than the paid endpoint.

- [Roster MCP - Hire an AI Agent by the Deliverable](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/roster-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://roster-ivory-zeta.vercel.app/api/mcp` where the usable half needs no credential: `initialize` **HTTP 200** in 0.23 to 0.55 seconds, `serverInfo` `roster` **1.0.0**, and `tools/list` returning all **23** tools with full schemas in **29,165** bytes. The product is a catalogue of named AI agents with a role, a biography, personality sliders, a `not_for` list and fixed price packages, and the workflow is a purchase rather than a prompt: `search_agents` on a launch-email brief returned **18** candidates out of the **58** the submission describes, `from_price_usd` from **30** to **50**, turnaround from **60 minutes** to **4 hours**, and a `match_reason` written as a sentence. `get_agent` on the top match returned three packages, **$35** for five product pages, **$40** for a three-email launch sequence and **$50** for one landing page. `get_sandbox_key` issued a working `rk_test_` key with no account, `daily_job_limit` **20** and `spend_limit_usd` **100**, stating that a sandbox job never reaches a real model and is never billed, and `hire_agent` with that key returned a completed job in **0.27** seconds with `package_selected_by: "brief_match"` choosing the three-email package at **$40** on its own, the other two returned as `alternatives` with prices and payment `charged: false`. `get_usage` then reported the key's own meter in timezone `America/New_York` with alert thresholds at **80** and **100** percent. **The reason it earns a guide is that nothing else here prices a deliverable before the work starts:** a live key is approved by a person through `request_access`, every key carries a daily job limit and a spend limit, each job includes two revisions, a rating goes on a public track record and `open_dispute` routes to a human. **Gap recorded:** no live hire was made, so real turnaround, revision quality and dispute handling are unexercised, and `rotate_webhook_secret`, `redeliver_webhook` and signature verification were not driven; sandbox output is a deterministic stand-in, useful as a rehearsal and useless for judging writing quality; and the endpoint is a Vercel deployment domain rather than a custom domain.
- [Markproof MCP - Watermark AI Output for Article 50](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/markproof-mcp/) - the first entry in this catalogue that treats machine readable marking of generated media as a tool call, and it arrives with a deadline a month away: the European AI Act implementation timeline puts the Article 50(2) obligations for providers generating synthetic audio, image, video or text at **2 August 2026** and requires content placed on the market before that date to be compliant by **2 December 2026**. The server is local stdio via `npx -y markproof-mcp`, MIT, published as `markproof-mcp` **0.3.1** with `mcpName` `io.github.Ajinkya710/markproof`, registering one server with three tools: `mark_file`, which watermarks and C2PA-signs a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, WAV or MP3 file, writes `<name>.marked.png` beside the original and returns a watermark code and a public verification URL, with an optional visible AI-generated label; `verify_file`, which checks any file for a watermark and a manifest and reports signature validity; and `get_asset`, free, which reads a record by id. The two marking tools cost one API call each. The two layer argument is the correct one: a watermark is a signal in the pixels or the waveform, a C2PA manifest is a tamper evident record that states what generated the file and breaks on any edit, and marking with one and not the other answers half the question. Plans are published plainly, Free at **$0** with **250** API calls a month, Indie at **$29** for **25,000**, Pro at **$79** for **100,000**, no card for the free key, files processed in the EU, and a free checker at `markproof.co/check` that needs no signup. **Gap recorded, and it is the largest this pass carries:** there is no hosted endpoint (`https://markproof.co/mcp` answered **404**) and `npx -y markproof-mcp` with no key printed `set MARKPROOF_API_KEY` and exited, so `initialize` and `tools/list` could not be run and the three tools are the published package rather than a driven list; watermark robustness, manifest validity, re-encoding survival and the accuracy of `verify_file` are unverified, the checker was not driven, text marking is outside the server, and `https://markproof.co/v1/assets` answered **404** from the static site.
- [SeatLayer MCP - Seating Charts Built by an Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/seatlayer-mcp/) - two servers, and the split is the story. `https://mcp.seatlayer.io/mcp` answered a keyless `initialize` with **HTTP 401** in 0.28 seconds and `{"error":"unauthorized","code":"bad_designer_session"}`, the normal state for an OAuth-only surface carrying **63** tools behind a per-administrator grant, while the sibling at `https://docs.seatlayer.io/mcp` answered **200** keyless with `serverInfo` `seatlayer-knowledge` **0.109.1** and **11** tools whose instructions ask the client to quote the canonical URLs every result returns. Three calls were made against it in 0.06 to 0.08 seconds each: `pricing` returned one prepaid credit per confirmed sold seat with designing, rendering, browsing, holds and releases consuming nothing, the first production payment at **$0**, **100** free sold-seat credits per organization per calendar month, credits that never expire and a ladder from **500** credits at **$50** (**10** cents a seat) to **100,000** at **$5,000** (**5** cents), with hosted ticketing a separate wallet at **$0.50** per confirmed ticket paying into the organizer's own gateway; `capabilities`, reviewed **2026-09-27**, separates released from unreleased in the vendor's own matrix with buyer 3D released behind a 2D fallback, **51** templates of which **35** carry 3D relief, and SDKs across web, seven server languages, four mobile platforms and REST OpenAPI 3.1; `product_overview` records the scale as fixtures rather than adjectives, public demos at a **200,000** seat stadium and a **100,000** seat arena and a readiness observation dated **2026-09-14** on a **53,018** seat chart. **The design is why the guide exists:** an administrator approves each connection on a consent screen, narrows it to one chart or a workspace and ticks capabilities individually, every call using an event capability re-checks that the person who connected the agent still holds a role allowing it in the dashboard, writing to an event on sale takes a plan the person approves where a yes covers that plan only and held and sold seats never change, an administrator gets a digest at most every 15 minutes per agent, and a publish can be undone in one click. **Gap recorded:** no grant exists, so all **63** tools are the vendor's documentation rather than a `tools/list` response, chart building, tracing, validation, publishing and live event control are unexercised, the **200,000** and **100,000** seat demos and the **53,018** seat observation were not loaded, and `compare_with` and `renderer_evidence` were not called.
